results.title: Shunt-capacitor impedance: +3V3
results.summary: Actual ngspice AC solution of an estimated capacitor network. Adding 100 nF changes impedance by 13.3 dB lower at the baseline peak (500 MHz).
assumptions: Small-signal 1 A AC current at U1 pad 1; voltage magnitude equals impedance in ohms.
Nominal capacitor values; each capacitor has assumed ESR 0.03 ohm and ESL 0.8 nH.
Connection inductance uses a rough 0.7 nH/mm rule of thumb; it is not a field-extracted parasitic model.
Only the listed capacitor branches are modeled; regulator, IC, plane spreading, shared-path coupling and cable impedances are omitted.
Comparison adds 100 nF at the port with an assumed 1 mm connection and the same ESR/ESL.
C1: measured signal route 1.79 mm; return distance estimated at 4.8 mm (plane/current path unresolved).
warnings: Estimated passive-network impedance, not radiated emissions or a compliance result.
DC bias, capacitor tolerances and frequency-dependent losses are not characterized.
Full IC and custom behavioral models are not executed. A completed passive comparison does not validate the whole circuit or any custom IC model.
The proposed change worsens the response by up to 4.7 dB elsewhere in this band.

results.title: Passive LC stage: L1
results.summary: Actual ngspice AC solution of an isolated passive stage. Adding 22 ohm changes output by 3.1 dB lower at the baseline peak, under the stated source/load assumptions.
assumptions: Isolated small-signal stage from SW through L1 to +5V; source 50 ohm and load 50 ohm are assumptions.
Nominal component values, capacitor ESR 0.03 ohm and ESL 0.8 nH; connections treated as ideal.
Comparison adds 22 ohm in series with L1.
All other connected circuitry is omitted; this is a local topology experiment, not full-circuit simulation.
Inductor uses an ideal inductance and assumed 0.1 ohm winding resistance; self-resonance and saturation are unknown.
warnings: Compare attenuation only within the frequency range where these lumped component assumptions are valid.
Added resistance can cause DC voltage drop, heating and slower signals; load current and timing must be checked before applying.
This does not predict regulator stability, switching waveforms or radiated emissions.

results.title: CLK24: local trace field simulation
results.summary: openEMS simulated a 25.00 mm straight section and compared 50 Ω and 72 Ω loads. Lower S11 means less reflection in this simplified model.
assumptions: Local 25.00 mm section of CLK24 on F.Cu; bends, remaining route and component models are excluded.
0.300 mm trace over 0.200 mm FR4, relative permittivity 4.2.
Broad ideal reference plane at In1.Cu/GND; filled copper continuity was checked within at least six dielectric heights.
Zero-thickness perfect conductors; solder mask, conductor loss, roughness, connector/package parasitics and distant conductors are omitted.
Dielectric loss is approximated by constant conductivity matching the saved loss tangent at half the maximum frequency.
Ports are synthetic resistive terminations, not verified on-board driver/receiver circuits. This is a field-solver screening result, not absolute radiated emissions or a compliance result.
Mesh size is bounded; mesh-refinement convergence has not been established for this board.
At least 30 dB of energy decay is required. Very small reflections and small differences may be numerical error and need a refined model before quantitative interpretation.
Synthetic source resistance 50 Ω; baseline load 50 Ω; compared load 72 Ω.
recommendations: The compared resistance does not clearly reduce worst-case reflection. Review the complete route and actual driver/receiver impedances before changing termination.
Confirm promising changes with circuit simulation and a measurement; these port curves do not predict an EMI compliance margin.
